content:
iPadOS and macOS used to be two completely different software platforms. However, since the launch of iPadOS 26, especially this year, the two have become increasingly similar. iPadOS 27 adds three features that bring the iPad closer to the Mac than ever before.

#1: Status Bar Shows App Name

I personally use an M5 iPad Pro, paired with the Magic Keyboard at all times. Keyboard users have always faced one problem: the iPad lacks a clear indicator of the "active app."

If there's only one app on screen, that's not an issue. But if you have several apps open at once, keyboard shortcuts become very difficult to manage. I can't count how many times I've expected a shortcut to trigger in one app, only for it to fire in another.

The Mac solved this problem a long time ago by placing the active app's name in the upper-left corner of the screen. Now iPadOS 27 has followed suit.

iPadOS 27 users will see the active app's name in the status bar, right next to the time, date, and other elements. It's a small change, but it's extremely welcome and dramatically improves the keyboard experience on iPad.

#2: Permanently Visible Menu Bar

Another welcome iPadOS 27 change is the option to permanently display the menu bar.

Apple brought the menu bar to the iPad for the first time last year. However, unlike on the Mac, the iPadOS 26 menu bar only appeared when the user actively summoned it.

In iPadOS 27, the Settings app has added a toggle under "Multitasking & Gestures" that reads: "Auto-show and hide menu bar."

Turning this option off keeps the menu bar visible at all times. I've been using this setting throughout the iPadOS beta period — it's one of my favourite changes this year.

#3: Everyday Operations Feel Closer to Mac Speed

Although I love my iPad and appreciate the new features in iPadOS 26 and 27, I sometimes get frustrated by how slow some basic operations are. For example, earlier this year I wrote: "Using the right-click on iPadOS feels so slow and laggy, but on the Mac it's instant."

Thanks to Apple's focus on squashing bugs this year, I'm happy to report that iPadOS 27 has improved in speed for these kinds of everyday tasks.

Apple says context menus with mouse input now open faster — I've definitely felt this myself. Browsing files and transferring them to an external drive is now "up to 5x faster," according to Apple, matching the speed of Finder on Mac. Apps launch more quickly, and window management is smoother when closing, switching, or dragging windows.

There are still areas where the Mac is faster than the iPad, and the latter can still feel sluggish at times. But overall, the speed improvements in iPadOS 27 are a significant step in the right direction.

What are your favourite new features and changes in iPadOS 27? Let us know in the comments.
